title: Explaining Concept Shift with Interpretable Feature Attribution
anchored_claims: SGShift-KA (sparse GAM with knockoffs and absorption term) achieves AUC greater than 0.9 for identifying shifted features across semi-synthetic benchmarks, outperforming the Diff, WhyShift, and SHAP-difference baselines by 2-3x in recall (Table 2).
On the Diabetes Readmission dataset (73,615 samples, 33 features, split by ER vs. non-ER admission), SGShift variants detect true shifted features with recall exceeding 80-90% (Table 2).

Sample-efficiency experiments show SGShift's knockoff variants (SGShift-K, SGShift-KA) retain top detection performance even when the number of samples available from the shifted (target) domain is small (Figure 1).

On the COVID-19 Hospitalizations dataset (16,187 samples, 30 features, split pre/post-Omicron) and the SUPPORT2 dataset (9,105 samples, 64 features, split by survival vs. death outcome), SGShift's real-world validation shows an elbow-shaped performance curve indicating that only a sparse subset of features accounts for the concept shift (Figure 2).
SGShift variants consistently outperform the Diff, WhyShift, and SHAP baselines across both matched and mismatched model-specification configurations (Table 2).
